- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) recently, model often overreacts to short-term spikes; cap upward momentum or adjust downward.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5-10 days; apply downward correction of 1-2%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 10-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10-20% if sentiment is weak or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict late-period prices (last 7-10 days); apply smoothing or lagged decay factor (e.g., 0.85 multiplier for final 5 days).
